label: Рота
description: A 10-sentence usage card for рота (company; unit).

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Рота' stays in the nominative as the subject of 'стоит'. 'Наша' is the agreeing feminine possessive, and 'на границе' gives the location. A basic military statement.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Роту' is the accusative direct object of 'построил'. 'Командир' is the nominative subject doing the lining up, and 'утром' adds the time. A common drill scene.
Strategic focus: Prepositional location. 'В роте' uses the prepositional form 'роте' after 'в' to mean within the unit. 'Нет мест' is a genitive of absence. Useful for capacity talk.
Strategic focus: Genitive of belonging. 'Роты' is the genitive after 'из', marking which unit the soldiers come from. 'Нашей' agrees in the feminine genitive. A natural origin phrase.
Strategic focus: Instrumental with command verb. 'Ротой' is the instrumental required by 'командует', the verb of commanding. 'Два года' gives the duration. A clean instrumental-government model.
Strategic focus: Dative recipient. 'Роте' is the dative, the unit receiving the order. 'Новое задание' is the nominative thing given by the impersonal 'дали'. Good for assignment language.
Strategic focus: Genitive singular after a numeral. 'Роты' takes the genitive singular form required after 'три'. 'В лагере' is the prepositional location. A useful counting pattern.

Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Роты' is the nominative plural as the subject of 'вернулись'. 'Все' agrees in the plural, and 'в часть' is the accusative of destination. Shows the plural.
Strategic focus: Prepositional of service. 'В этой роте' uses the prepositional 'роте' after 'в' to name where one served. 'Этой' agrees in the feminine prepositional. A personal-history phrase.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural. 'Рот' is the bare genitive plural after 'командиров', naming the commanders of the companies. 'Вызвали' is the impersonal plural verb. A staff-level phrase.
